evidence.exact_quote: Decision_Log is a human-authored decision ledger, not a derived decision log. `Plans/auto_decisions.jsonl` is pipeline-managed and must not be hand-edited here; `Plans/.pipeline/research_packet.json` (`/.pipeline/research_packet.json`) is regenerated after owner/consumer reconciliation and must not be treated as fidelity-complete Decision_Log canon.

items.impact: Establishes which decision records are human-authored canon and prevents generated pipeline artifacts from silently acquiring equal authority.
items.statement: The prologue explicitly separates the authoritative human decision ledger from pipeline-managed auto-decisions and the regenerated research packet.
items.title: Human decision-ledger authority boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Decision_Log remains human-authored and final for its recorded decisions.

items.impact: Builders have a direct oracle for preserving the ledger's authorship and finality boundary.
items.statement: DL-002 binds decision finality to the human-authored Decision_Log and separately excludes pipeline artifacts from that role.
items.title: DL-002 fixes decision-ledger authority

evidence.exact_quote: - OpenCode_Deep_Extraction.md mapping remains a reference aid only.

items.impact: External extraction structure cannot override local subsystem ownership.
items.statement: DL-003 makes OpenCode extraction mapping advisory and leaves final subsystem ownership with local Puppet Master contracts.
items.title: DL-003 limits extraction-map authority

evidence.exact_quote: - Section-number drift in extraction source does not propagate into local SSOT docs.

items.impact: Local references remain stable when the extraction source is renumbered.
items.statement: DL-004 supplies an explicit anti-propagation constraint for source section-number drift.
items.title: DL-004 blocks section-number drift propagation

evidence.exact_quote: - The node graph is the canonical orchestration model.

items.impact: Execution implementations cannot substitute a non-graph orchestration ontology.
items.statement: DL-005 defines the node graph as canonical, graph-owns Feature Seam and Work Package, and fixes Node as the smallest executable unit.
items.title: DL-005 establishes the graph execution ontology

evidence.exact_quote: - Runtime owns readiness, blockers, transitions, retries, and dispatch.

items.impact: Concurrent overseer challenges and runtime transitions can be implemented with incompatible precedence, retry, and cancellation behavior.
items.statement: DL-006 assigns runtime ownership and separates overseer roles, but does not define the arbitration protocol when an overseer challenge races a runtime-owned transition, retry, or dispatch.
items.title: DL-006 omits runtime-versus-overseer arbitration

evidence.exact_quote: - Locally Complete, Available to Seam, and Seam Complete remain distinct.

items.impact: Distinct labels alone do not prevent illegal promotion, premature seam completion, or inconsistent reopen behavior.
items.statement: DL-007 names three distinct completion states but does not define entry predicates, allowed edges, revocation edges, or rejection oracles for invalid transitions.
items.title: DL-007 names states without a transition contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Weak integration includes runtime/GUI mismatch, contract mismatch, workflow gaps, and architecture drift.

items.impact: Local technical success cannot hide cross-layer GUI, contract, workflow, or architectural integration defects.
items.statement: DL-008 explicitly makes weak integration first-class and enumerates four defect families including runtime/GUI mismatch.
items.title: DL-008 makes weak integration first-class

evidence.exact_quote: - High-impact claims use deterministic 2-of-3 corroboration.

items.impact: Implementations can disagree about who votes, duplicate-voter identity, deadline behavior, replacement voters, and when the outcome becomes final.
items.statement: DL-009 fixes the numeric threshold but leaves voter eligibility, independence, deduplication, timeout, partial-response, and concurrent-finalization rules unspecified.
items.title: DL-009 lacks an executable 2-of-3 protocol

evidence.exact_quote: - Graph patching creates a new graph generation.

items.impact: A crash or competing patch can expose mixed generations, orphan lineage, or duplicate generation numbers without a defined repair path.
items.statement: DL-010 requires a new generation and visible superseded paths but does not define transactional publication, concurrency control, idempotency, rollback, or partial-write recovery.
items.title: DL-010 omits graph-patch atomicity

evidence.exact_quote: - Source Control stays worktree-first and compact.

items.impact: Source Control avoids absorbing orchestration-specific lane, package, and seam context.
items.statement: DL-011 assigns compact worktree concerns to Source Control and operational lane, package, and seam context to Orchestrator.
items.title: DL-011 separates Source Control from Orchestrator context

evidence.exact_quote: - Actor types do not collapse into one ontology.

items.impact: Shared identity fields do not erase actor-specific authorization, behavior, or audit meaning.
items.statement: DL-012 explicitly spans named runtime actors while prohibiting an ontology collapse among them.
items.title: DL-012 preserves actor distinctions in shared identity

evidence.exact_quote: - Blocked approval identity is anchored by run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, and optional attempt_id.

items.impact: Approvals for separate attempts can collide or be replayed against the wrong attempt when attempt_id is absent.
items.statement: DL-013 makes attempt_id optional without defining when omission is safe, how attempt identity is reconstructed, or how stale and duplicate approvals are rejected.
items.title: DL-013 leaves optional attempt identity unsafe

evidence.exact_quote: - resume_url remains serialized transport only.

items.impact: Consumers cannot treat a transport URL as the canonical navigation identity.
items.statement: DL-014 cleanly separates route_target, OpenSubject, and resume_url into navigation, identity-native open, and serialized transport roles.
items.title: DL-014 defines navigation primitive boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: - Secrets in logs, PII, and diff fatigue are planned for up front.

items.impact: Sensitive evidence may remain over-retained, become undeletable, or leak when allowlisting or redaction fails.
items.statement: DL-015 requires allowlisted or structured capture but does not define redaction failure behavior, retention and deletion periods, access control, encryption, export policy, or a purge oracle for secrets and PII.
items.title: DL-015 leaves sensitive debug-evidence lifecycle undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - actor_kind and execution_role are preserved for non-run auditability and replay.

items.impact: Non-run actors can be recorded but still replay under the wrong account, privilege, or actor scope, especially after partial provider-selection failure.
items.statement: DL-016 requires actor_kind and execution_role and rejects run-only storage keys, but does not define envelope identity, authorization scoping, uniqueness, mutation, retention, provider-selection failure, or replay validation rules.
items.title: DL-016 lacks an executable provider actor-envelope contract

evidence.exact_quote: - sharding_config and auto_decisions do not disagree on fallback chunk-line settings.

items.impact: A detector can identify disagreement yet different tools can choose different winners or race while rewriting the same support state.
items.statement: DL-017 forbids chunk-line disagreement but does not identify the authoritative value, normalization algorithm, repair owner, lock or ordering model, or observable failure result.
items.title: DL-017 detects support drift without defining reconciliation

evidence.exact_quote: - /labels, /action, /runtime, and /object consumers do not invent alternate peer terms.

items.impact: Runtime, actions, objects, and visible labels share one vocabulary rather than drifting into peer synonyms.
items.statement: DL-018 establishes canonical user-facing and runtime vocabulary and explicitly forbids alternate peer terms across named consumers.
items.title: DL-018 fixes governance copy across consumers

evidence.exact_quote: - Newly discovered work becomes remediation nodes or graph-patch requests.

items.impact: Overseers cannot smuggle discovered work into hidden execution; it must enter explicit graph governance.
items.statement: DL-019 defines graph-owned run, package, seam, and node semantics and routes discovered work through remediation nodes or patch requests.
items.title: DL-019 keeps governance and discovered work graph-owned

evidence.exact_quote: - Weak integration concerns are grouped under readable headings including Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, and Design.

items.impact: A UI can satisfy the headings while misleading users during empty, loading, stale, degraded, offline, high-volume, inaccessible, or localized presentations.
items.statement: DL-020 requires visible grouped summaries but omits aggregation and ordering rules, empty/loading/error/stale/offline states, overflow limits, accessibility semantics, localization behavior, and a falsifiable visual oracle.
items.title: DL-020 leaves weak-integration summary states underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, and Reopened by New Evidence remain explicit named states.

items.impact: Different consumers can produce illegal edges, conflicting reopen reasons, duplicate transitions, or contradictory blocked and recovery displays.
items.statement: DL-021 enumerates lifecycle states and visible blocked context but does not supply allowed edges, guards, actor authority, idempotency, concurrent-event precedence, rollback, or invalid-transition oracles.
items.title: DL-021 names lifecycle states without their machine

evidence.exact_quote: - Gate/evidence schema mismatch is exposed as first-class governance defect.

items.impact: A stale or forged approval can mutate the wrong blocked episode, and a detected schema defect can strand the gate without a deterministic recovery path.
items.statement: DL-022 specifies anchor fields and defect visibility but not approval authentication, freshness, single-use semantics, duplicate or concurrent decision handling, mismatch quarantine, operator remediation, or resumption criteria.
items.title: DL-022 omits approval replay protection and defect recovery

evidence.exact_quote: - Contracts_V0 compatibility notes for request-centric to blocked-episode migration are preserved.

items.impact: Mixed-version clients and persisted requests can be dropped, double-applied, or indefinitely accepted through the deprecated identity path.
items.statement: DL-023 declares the target identity and compatibility-note preservation but not the activation condition, data backfill, dual-read or dual-write period, conflict precedence, telemetry, cutoff, rollback, or legacy rejection oracle.
items.title: DL-023 lacks a safe blocked-identity migration sequence

evidence.exact_quote: - No 2-of-3 means a high-impact claim is not accepted as blocking or canonical truth.

items.impact: No-response, dissent, duplicate identity, late vote, and replacement-voter cases can yield inconsistent blocking truth or advisory visibility.
items.statement: DL-024 defines accepted and non-accepted outcomes but omits evaluator selection, vote identity, deadline and no-quorum behavior, late-result precedence, concurrent finalization, advisory deduplication, and scale limits.
items.title: DL-024 leaves corroboration edge outcomes undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - /Clamped and /Removed remain aliases only where explicitly documented.

items.impact: Related links and aliases can be rendered inconsistently, point to ambiguous targets, fail offline, or become unusable for keyboard, assistive-technology, and localized users.
items.statement: DL-025 enumerates link clusters and alias limits but not target identity, directionality, ordering, broken-target behavior, offline behavior, accessibility semantics, localization, or test oracles.
items.title: DL-025 lists help clusters without interaction semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - Lane cleanup may transition to retained instead of immediate cleanup under the listed review, promotion, weak integration, concern, corroboration, or manual retention conditions.

items.impact: Lanes can remain retained forever or be destructively cleaned while an active retention reason still exists.
items.statement: DL-026 defines entry reasons for retained but not reason aggregation, authority to add or clear reasons, expiry, concurrent updates, exit predicates, cleanup resumption, rollback, or audit and notification oracles.
items.title: DL-026 has retained entry conditions but no exit contract

items.impact: The retired bridge claims auditable migration lineage while its in-place preservation fields contain visibly incomplete source statements, weakening exact human review and falsifiability.
items.statement: DL-001 correctly forbids re-owning atomized coverage, yet several negative-constraint and owner-boundary entries are truncated mid-sentence, so the compatibility lineage payload is not textually fidelity-complete in this document.
items.title: DL-001 retired-bridge lineage contains truncated source text

segments.summary: The prologue and DL-002 through DL-005 provide strong authority and anti-drift boundaries; DL-006 and DL-007 leave arbitration and executable completion-transition rules open.
DL-008, DL-011, DL-012, and DL-014 set clear scope boundaries; the corroboration, graph-patch, optional-attempt, and sensitive-debug-evidence contracts omit failure, race, and lifecycle behavior.

DL-018 and DL-019 preserve vocabulary and graph ownership; actor-envelope, support reconciliation, seam-summary, lifecycle-machine, approval replay, and evidence-defect recovery behavior remain materially underspecified.

The final window preserves migration, corroboration, help, and retention intentions, but lacks operational edge contracts; the retired DL-001 bridge also embeds visibly truncated preservation text despite claiming auditable lineage.
